text:
Nina: Heads up — rotated a project API key and our Go worker kept using the old key until restart. Streaming clients were fine, background cron jobs hit 401s.

Omar: Did the worker read env at startup or before each request? Go sampleapps currently read REDWOOD_API_KEY on init.

Nina: Read once at init. We deploy as long-lived binary, so rotation requires process restart.

Raj: This is a parity gap — Node/Python have credential provider hooks; Go does not. We should add a Provider interface: GetKey() and Subscribe(onChange).

Omar: Agree. Also noticed different env names across repos: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_TOKEN, RLW_API_KEY. We should pick one canonical name and alias the old ones with deprecation warnings.

Nina: Proposal: canonical REDWOOD_API_KEY for long-lived, REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN for ephemeral sessions. SDK precedence: explicit param > REDWOOD_SESSION_TOKEN > REDWOOD_API_KEY > session file (~/.config/redwood/active_session) > keyring.

Raj: For Go, I'll add a creds package that reads the session file and supports fsnotify to signal changes instead of polling. It can expose a Small Provider used by both sampleapps and SDKs.

Omar: Quick mitigation: add a note in onboarding and sampleapp README explaining rotation and show a tiny wrapper that recreates client on SIGHUP.

kenshi-bot: Created task DEVX-1982: "SDK parity: credential provider + canonical env names + sampleapp docs" and assigned to @raj.

Nina: Thanks — please also run a repo grep to find RLW_* and REDWOOD_TOKEN references. I'll coordinate with infra to add a console rotation checklist reminding owners to verify scopes (eg realtime:connect).
